beats.intent: ThinkSR keeps dense image features moving through encoder, windows, recurrent DQ-CTM ticks, and decoder.
beats.claim: ThinkSR end to end: encoder, windows, shared DQ-CTM ticks, decoder.
beats.narration: The method keeps a dense carrier while a compact thought process reads and updates it. The encoder starts from the low-resolution image. Windowing organizes the dense field for local processing. DQ-CTM runs shared ticks, so the same parameters recur through the thought process. The decoder turns the updated dense representation back into the super-resolved image.

params.headline: ThinkSR runs dense features through shared DQ-CTM ticks
params.note: The loop returns to the thought stage itself.

beats.intent: The carrier equation first builds a dense feature field, then partitions that field without dropping tokens.
beats.narration: The carrier is defined before the compact thought process acts on it. The encoder maps the low-resolution image into a dense feature field. The window partition produces tokens from that field while keeping every token in the carrier path.

params.headline: The carrier stays dense before windowed thought begins

terms.label: window partition of the dense field

beats.intent: DQ-CTM-SR is not the smallest model in the comparison; its parameter count is second largest among the five methods.
beats.narration: The parameter comparison shows that DQ-CTM-SR should not be described as cheap. CATANet is the smallest model at zero point five three five million parameters. RFDN is nearly the same size at zero point five five zero million. IMDN remains below one million parameters. DQ-CTM-SR has one point one two nine million parameters, which is the second largest of the five. CARN is larger, at one point five nine two million parameters.

params.headline: DQ-CTM-SR has the second largest parameter count here
params.note: Smallest first; DQ-CTM-SR is second largest.
